Questions, observational units, populations, samples, and evidence in context.

:::

**Topic 1.4 Graphical Representations for One Categorical Variable**

Build bar and pie charts, compare samples, and audit graphical claims.

**Topic 1.5 Graphical Representations for One Quantitative Variable**

Build dotplots, stem-and-leaf plots and histograms; explore how bin widths change a display.

[Open Topic 1.5 →](<Topic 1.5/topic-1-5.qmd>)
:::
::: {.route-card}
**Topic 1.6 Descriptions for One Quantitative Variable Distributions**

Describe shape, center, spread and unusual features using graphical evidence.

[Open Topic 1.6 →](<Topic 1.6/topic-1-6.qmd>)

::: {.route-card}
**Topic 1.7 Summary Statistics for One Quantitative Variable**

Learn mean, quartiles, variation, two outlier screens, and unit conversion through a linked dotplot and practice.

[Open Topic 1.7 →](<Topic 1.7/topic-1-7.qmd>)
:::

**Topic 1.8 Graphical Representations of Summary Statistics for One Quantitative Variable**

Construct five-number summaries and modified boxplots with a step-by-step linked graph; learn what a boxplot conceals and how mean and median relate to skewness.

[Open Topic 1.8 →](<Topic 1.8/topic-1-8.qmd>)
:::
::: {.route-card}

Compare distribution shapes and summaries on common scales, and calculate standardized relative positions with z-scores.

[Open Topic 1.9 →](<Topic 1.9/topic-1-9.qmd>)
:::

**Topic 1.10 The Investigative Question Revisited and Data Collection**

Build a precise statistical question, distinguish observational studies and experiments, and explore selection, treatment assignment, confounding and the limits of conclusions.

[Open Topic 1.10 →](<Topic 1.10/topic-1-10.qmd>)
:::
::: {.route-card}

## Keep the datasets distinct

The School A travel-method table has **40 responses**: Walk 8, Bicycle 6, Bus 18 and Car 8. The quantitative graph lessons use **24 one-way commute times**. Changing a display keeps its underlying observations the same.

<div data-chart="commute-dot" class="chart-frame"><p>Commute times: 5, 8, 10, 12, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 18, 20, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 30, 32, 35, 38, 42, 48, 58 minutes.</p></div>

Existing chapter addresses remain available. The editable Unit 1 chapters, data, code, and tests are organized in the repository's **Unit 1** folder, with one subfolder per topic and a **Shared** folder for material reused across topics.
